title: Mean Cosmic Microwave Background Photon Energy and Wavelength from Planck and Hubble Scales: Predictions, Observational Comparisons, and Constraints on H0
content: A recently proposed expression connects the present cosmic microwave background temperature to the Planck temperature, Planck length, and Hubble radius. In this note, we combine that temperature relation with the standard mean-energy formula for photons in a blackbody spectrum. This gives a direct formula for the mean cosmic microwave background photon energy in terms of the Planck and cosmological scales. Using the Particle Data Group value H0 = (67.4±0.5)kms−1 Mpc−1, the formula gives Tcmb = (2.7358 ± 0.0101)K and a mean photon energy of (1.02027 ± 0.00378) × 10−22 J, or (6.3680±0.0236)×10−4 eV. It also predicts a photon-number-weighted mean wavelength of (3.5984± 0.0133)mm and a wavelength associated with the mean photon energy of (1.9470 ± 0.0072)mm. The predicted mean energy is consistent, at approximately one propagated standard deviation, with the value calculated from the observed CMB temperature.
